title: Records show that in 1951, NRC was prepared across the country by 'copying' data from the Census schedules; the countrywide NRC was never published, except in undivided Assam, which at the time also included Manipur and Tripura
author: Vijaita Singh
content_html:
The Union government’s decision to advance the Population Enumeration phase of Census 2027 in four poll-bound States, coupled with the introduction of several new questions in the Census schedule, has prompted some former Census officials to raise concerns regarding the quality of data that is to be collected and the potential links between the Census, the National Population Register (NPR) and, ultimately, the National Register of Citizens (NRC).

There is a precedent for Census data having been used to prepare the NRC. Records show that this took place in 1951, during Independent India’s first Census, when the NRC was prepared across the country by "copying" data from the Census schedules. However, for unspecified reasons, a countrywide NRC was never published, except in undivided Assam, which at the time also included Manipur and Tripura.

Speaking to The Hindu, former Deputy Registrar General of India K. Narayanan Unni stressed that any link between the Census and population-registration activities remains speculative. However, some of the information being sought in the latest Census questionnaire resembled data collected during previous NPR updation exercises.

The NPR, first created in 2011 and initially proposed to be updated with the first phase of the now-scrapped Census 2021, has been put on the back burner due to stiff opposition from political parties and civil society groups, who had expressed concern that the data could be used to create a countrywide NRC amid allegations that the process could lead to a large number of people being left out of citizenship.

Mr. Unni said, “NPR is generated under the Citizenship Act, and data is supposed to be published. However, Census data is confidential and can only be used for statistical purposes. But in 1951, Census data was used to prepare the NRC in Assam...” He added that even though Census data is confidential, this doesn’t mean that the 1951 exercise of using it to prepare NRC won’t be repeated.

On August 14, 2026, the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India (RG&CCI) notified a set of 40 questions to be asked during the Population Enumeration phase, or the second phase, of the Census, adding 13 new questions or data fields that were not part of the 2011 Census questionnaire.

Some of the additional questions, such as particulars of a person’s parents, including their names, religion, place of birth, Aadhaar number, mobile phone number, voter ID and driving licence details, mirror those asked in the rehearsal form of the NPR in 2019.

The NPR had been updated in 2015 and already has the family-wise database of 119 crore residents.

The 1951 exercise

The 1951 Census report by R.B. Vaghaiwalla, the Superintendent of Census Operations for Assam, Manipur and Tripura, shows that the NRC was conceived primarily as a Census and administrative tool rather than a citizenship-verification exercise.

“An important innovation of this Census was the preparation of the NRC, in which all important Census data was transcribed from the Census slips. The Register uses the same symbols and abbreviations and is a copy of the Census slips,” the 1951 report said.

Missing NRC entries were copied from Census slips, and missing Census slips were recreated from NRC entries under a special reconciliation exercise undertaken by Vaghaiwalla. This took place even though there had been countrywide instructions from the Registrar General to limit such checks “in the interest of economy of time and money”.

According to Vaghaiwalla, the register was intended to be maintained permanently and updated by village officials, thereby providing continuity between Censuses. Though Section 15 of the Census Act, 1948 ensures confidentiality and says that “records of census [are] not open to inspection nor admissible in evidence”, the NRC was prepared using the data, establishing a precedent of using Census data to prepare the register.

A former Census official, speaking on the condition of anonymity, said the NPR and the Census were legally distinct exercises governed by different laws. The official pointed out that the updation of the NRC in Assam in 2019 was not based on NPR data and required a separate data collection exercise.

Undercounting concerns

On September 5, the RG&CCI advanced the Population Enumeration phase of Census 2027 in the poll-bound States of Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Uttarakhand and Goa, while deferring the exercise in violence-hit Manipur. The Census will also be the first in Independent India to enumerate castes beyond Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

Mr. Unni said that the decision to conduct the Census in four States ahead of the rest of the country could lead to under-enumeration of migrant workers, particularly from Uttar Pradesh.

“Census dates were traditionally fixed around March 1 because migration was relatively low during that period. Advancing the exercise in States that are due to hold Assembly elections may mean that several migrant workers return home to vote and are not available where they ordinarily reside. By the time they reach their home State, enumeration there may already be over, creating the possibility that some migrants are not counted at either place," he said.

Other than these four States, as well as Ladakh and snow-bound areas of Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Jammu and Kashmir, population enumeration in the rest of the country will take place in February 2027 with a reference date of March 1, 2027. Snow-bound areas have traditionally been counted before the rest of the country.

India follows a de facto system of enumeration, under which a person is counted where he or she is present during the Census period. Mr. Unni said that even a small increase in undercounting could affect data quality because past Censuses have already recorded some degree of under-enumeration.

On the government’s decision to defer the Census in Manipur, he said that conducting the enumeration without public cooperation would compromise data quality. However, he argued that postponement could deprive the State of demographic evidence relevant to claims about migration and population change.

‘Respondent fatigue’

Mr. Unni questioned the utility of some of the new questions, particularly those relating to identity documents and vaccination history. “Many of these details are already available in administrative databases. It is not clear what statistical purpose some of these questions will serve,” he said.

He also cautioned that a lengthy questionnaire could increase “respondent fatigue” and create practical difficulties for enumerators, most of whom are government school teachers.

“If a household is required to answer dozens of questions for every family member, it will increase the time taken per household and may lead to resistance, particularly in urban areas where enumerators are often unknown to residents,” he said.

The other former Census official raised questions over the inclusion of Aadhaar details in Census 2027, noting that the collection of Aadhaar numbers may require changes to existing legal provisions.

title: ‘All parties are treated equally in SC’, CJI says in Rahul Gandhi case
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
Chief Justice of India Surya Kant on Wednesday (September 9, 2026) assured that “all parties are treated equally” in the Supreme Court after senior advocate and BJP spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia, appearing for a complainant in a defamation case against Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, alleged that the Opposition leader’s matter is being repeatedly adjourned.

The exchange happened during an oral mentioning by Mr. Bhatia to de-tag Mr. Gandhi’s plea against criminal proceedings arising from his alleged remarks concerning the Army and the Chinese attack in the context of the 2020 Galwan clash.

He said the last time the case was listed was in December last year. At the time, the top court had scheduled the next hearing on April 22, 2026. However, the case had not been listed until September 9.

Mr. Bhatia alleged the case was not being listed due to the “person mentioned”, and he should not be treated like a “VVIP”. He said Mr. Gandhi’s side was indulging in “dilatory tactics” to avoid a hearing.

Advocate Prasanna S., for Mr. Gandhi, vehemently objected to the submissions made by Mr. Bhatia, saying that such statements should not be permitted to be made in court.

“All parties are treated equally here,” Chief Justice Kant addressed Mr. Bhatia.

The Bench advised Mr. Bhatia to submit an application for de-tagging of the case.

The court had earlier stayed proceedings against Mr. Gandhi in the case based on a complaint filed by a retired Border Roads Organisation (BRO) officer, Uday Shankar Shrivastava, before a Lucknow Magistrate court in August 2023. The Lucknow court had issued summons to the Congress leader in February 2025.

Mr. Gandhi’s appeal to quash the summons had been declined by the Allahabad High Court in May 2025, compelling Mr. Gandhi to approach the Supreme Court in a special leave petition.

title: DMK declares Sethu Selvam as candidate for Thattanchavady bypoll
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
The Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam has declared K. Sethu Selvam as party candidate for the October 6 bypoll in Thattanchavady Assembly constituency in Puducherry.

Mr. Selvam, a former member of the Communist Party of India (CPI), had met former Chief Minister and DMK president M.K. Stalin on Wednesday at Chennai before his candidature was announced by the party. 

As the CPI candidate in 2021 Assembly polls, Mr Selvam had come second in Thattanchavady constituency fighting against Chief Minister and AINRC founder N. Rangasamy. He had garnered around 32% of votes in the 2021 election.

Following his expulsion from CPI in 2025 over allegations of financial impropriety, Mr. Selvam contested as an Independent from Thattanchavady during the April 2026 polls.

He came third by garnering around 17 % of the votes pushing Member of Parliament and PCC chief V. Vaithilingam to the fourth place.

title: Congress appoints Madhu Yaskhi Goud for All India Professional Congress
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
Former Lok Sabha member from Telangana, Madhu Yaskhi Goud, has been appointed new chairperson of the All India Professional Congress, the party wing that engaged with professionals.

A statement from Congress general secretary (organisation) said he replaces Praveen Chakravarty, who is now a Rajya Sabha member from Tamil Nadu.

The appointment, made by Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge, was announced in a statement.

“The party appreciates the contributions of outgoing Chairperson, Shri Praveen Chakravarty,” it said.

title: Punjab govt. employees call off their strike after assurance
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
Punjab government employees, primarily ministerial staff, withdrew their pen-down strike on Wednesday (September 9, 2026) following an assurance from the Chief Secretary that disciplinary show-cause notices against them would be revoked.

The employees, who had on Tuesday observed a day-long strike, were demanding that the government withdraw its letter branding their August 27 mass casual leave taken in protest as “unauthorised leave”.

The employees were on strike on the call given by Sanjha Mulazam Manch, Punjab, an organisation representing employees of Directorates in Chandigarh and Mohali, as well as all government offices across the State. They had declared that if their demand was not accepted, they will continue the strike till September 11. The State government had even decided to implement ‘no work, no pay’ in a bid to clamp down on the protest.

On Wednesday, a meeting was held between representatives of the manch and Chief Secretary K.A.P. Sinha here.

“We were assured that the notices will be withdrawn, and ‘no work, no pay’ would also not be implemented,” manch leader Sushil Kumar Fauji told The Hindu.

The stand-off between the employees and the government started on August 27, when over three lakh government employees launched a Statewide strike over their demands, which include restoring the Old Pension Scheme, release of pending 18% dearness allowance and regularisation of contractual employees, among others. A meeting between Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann and employees’ organisation representatives was called off after Mr. Mann insisted talks could only happen once the strike was withdrawn.

“We have also been assured that a meeting with the Chief Minister will be fixed over our other demands soon,” said Mr. Kumar.

title: ‘Why nine accused in Palghar doctor assault case are absconding?’: Bombay HC raps police
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
Bombay High Court on Wednesday (September 9, 2026) rapped Palghar police over laxity in probing the case against Shiv Sena workers for assault on medical staff and vandalising a private hospital in the district.

Bombay HC Bench comprising Justices A S Gadkari and Kamal Khata was hearing the suo-motu case with allegations that the police have failed to carry investigation in the case. 

A day before, Bombay HC ordered to summon the Palghar Superintendent of Police over the inaction allegations against the Shiv Sena workers. Palghar Superintendent of Police Yatish Deshmukh informed court that among the 10 accused named in the FIR, Shiv Sena city chief Rahul Gharat has been arrested, while remaining are absconding. 

In response, Court asked, “Why there was no prompt arrest? It is because of police’s laxity the accused are absconding.”

Calling the police action “unacceptable”, Court observed that police has failed to learn from previous incident in July where a doctor was assaulted in Thane District’s Dombivli region’s public hospital. 

In both the Palghar doctor assault case and the Thane case, Shiv Sena office bearers have been the accused. In case of Thane, Shiv Sena corporator Ramesh Mhatre was arrested.

Court said, “Was Thane incident not enough for police to learn a lesson?” Court also advised Palghar police to transfer the case to Mumbai police’s crime branch, if they are unable to take action.

On the night of September 5, Shiv Sena workers, the son of MLA Rajendra Gavit and deputy taluka chief Rohit Gavit allegedly assaulted staff at Relief Hospital in Palghar over expensive treatment. The incident was flagged during the hearing of suo motu case in Thane incident.

title: 15 workers rescued, 12 hospitalised after iron slab collapses at construction site in Gandhinagar
author: PTI
content_html:
Fifteen workers were rescued after a metal slab collapsed at site under construction in the Kudasan area of Gandhinagar on Wednesday (September 9, 2026) night, Gujarat Deputy Chief Minister Harsh Sanghavi said, adding that the debris-clearing operation would continue through the night to ensure that no one remained trapped.

Mr. Sanghavi said 12 of the rescued workers were admitted to Gandhinagar Civil Hospital, while three others who did not suffer major injuries were discharged.

“According to the report received just five minutes ago from the Gandhinagar Civil Hospital Superintendent, all 12 individuals currently hospitalised are safe, and none are in critical condition,” he said at the accident site.

The accident occurred around 9 p.m. at the an construction site in the Kudasan area of Gandhinagar when a large metal slab collapsed during ongoing construction work.

According to the Gandhinagar police control room, firefighters, police and the local administration were carrying out rescue operations at the site as labourers claimed that several persons were working on the metal structure and might have been trapped in the debris.

More than four fire brigades rushed to the spot after being alerted about the incident and launched a rescue operation. Ambulances were also deployed to provide immediate medical assistance to those rescued.

"Five persons have been shifted at the hospital for treatment so far. A team of doctors is taking care of them. Some of them have received fractures on their back and on leg. Doctors will take a call if there is need to operate them," Health Minister Praful Pansheriya told reporters at the Gandhinagar Civil hospital.

A firefighter said that a large crane and electric cutters were being used to remove the metal debris and check whether other workers were still trapped underneath.

The exact number of workers trapped under the collapsed metal structure was not immediately clear, officials said.

The exact number of workers trapped under the collapsed metal structure was not immediately clear, officials said.

title: 1,169 candidates set to win unopposed in Tripura village committee elections
author: Syed Sajjad Ali
content_html:
A record number of candidates contesting the upcoming village committee elections under the Tripura Tribal Areas Autonomous District Council are set to win unopposed owing to the lack of rival nominations.

The State Election Commission (SEC) said on Wednesday that polling will not be held in 1,169 seats, accounting for one-third of the 4,597 seats across 587 village committees, because only solitary nominations have been received. The SEC said scrutiny of all the 10,958 nominations filed was conducted during the day.

Most of the candidates set to win unopposed belong to the Tipra Motha. The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), the Tipra Motha, and the Indigenous People’s Front of Tripura had earlier announced that they would jointly contest the elections. However, the three parties have failed to arrive at a seat-sharing formula so far. A senior Minister said the alliance is nothing but an arrangement to keep the CPI(M) and the Congress at bay.

Contesting same seats

The Tipra Motha and the BJP have even fielded candidates for the same seats in several village committees. September 10 is the last date for withdrawal of nominations.

The SEC assured that the elections would be held in a peaceful manner on September 28. It added that the Ministry of Home Affairs has sanctioned 24 companies of Central forces to be deployed in sensitive areas in the State.
